method.filtering_summary: The live search pulled 2,785 postings; 1,796 were older than 7 days, 94 were reposts of listings over 30 days old, 255 were senior or excluded titles, 272 were not target roles, 176 failed Kenya eligibility, 38 were already applied to and 41 were duplicates. ReliefWeb failed in the automated search (parse error) and the automated Wellfound fetch is disabled by design, so Wellfound is recorded as failed there; the signed-in browser pass covered it instead (about 2,129 listings seen, about 25 read, 2 kept). Jobgether returned 569 roles and 236 fresh; 35 passed the filters, but the ones I opened list Turkey and Georgia, or ask 4+ years with US business hours, or need Monday.com experience, so none were kept; the rest are Europe or UK lists that do not name Kenya. micro1 returned 66 roles and 12 fresh, 6 kept and 1 new: the new one is an engineering-professor education task, so there is nothing new for Ben there. Browser passes (signed in, 26 Nov): Wellfound (2 kept: Grist shortlisted, Azodha dropped because it needs US work authorisation), Fuzu (about 661 listings, 1 kept) and the MyJobMag personalised feed (about 125 pulled, 2 kept). Syd Life AI's Junior Software Engineer (within 3 hours of UK time) was left out because Ben applied to it on 24 Nov. BeyondTrust's role is tagged Anywhere in the World on We Work Remotely, but the text says fully remote within the UK, so it is dropped. Canonical's Observability role was re-checked against the Greenhouse API. Other new roles that passed the automated filters but were not opened are listed as unchecked.

stories.title: Ant Group releases Ling-3.2-air, an MIT-licensed multimodal model for tool-using agents
stories.summary: Weights are out under the MIT licence: 124 billion parameters in total with 5.5 billion activated per token, with SGLang and vLLM deployment instructions. Ant reports AutomationBench-AA task completion rising from 15.7% to 61%.
stories.why: An open-weights model aimed at agents that finish office and browser tasks with tools, which is the kind of workflow he builds in n8n.

stories.title: Amazon Transcribe Turbo enters public preview with turn-taking for voice agents
stories.summary: Streaming word error rate drops about 14% relative in English; semantic turn-taking responds in about 615 ms with a 5% interruption rate; runtime ASR hints raise English menu-routing accuracy from 87% to 97%. The preview is in US East (Ohio).
stories.why: Voice-agent plumbing (turn detection, per-turn hints) is something a webhook-and-API engineer could wire into customer-support flows.

stories.title: Amini releases Soma-1X Lite, a 2B open-weight model for document intelligence
stories.summary: It scores 84.7 on olmOCR-Bench, runs about 15,000 pages an hour on one GPU at an estimated $0.22 per 1,000 pages, and had the lowest average error rate of five open models on ten African languages including Swahili.
stories.why: An African team shipping a small open model that reads Swahili documents, relevant to document-ingestion pipelines like his Kwara loan one.

stories.title: Maple raises $5.3M seed for private AI chat and a desktop agent
stories.summary: Epic Ventures led the round; models run inside trusted execution environments so Maple cannot read user data, and the team of four says it is actively hiring.
stories.why: A small agentic-AI company that is hiring, with an open-source trust model he could read and learn from.

stories.title: Permut raises EUR 3M seed for conversational AI agents that handle support and sales
stories.summary: The agents handle 80-85% of support enquiries without a human and run on web, WhatsApp, Instagram, Messenger and email; the team will grow from nine to 20 people.
stories.why: Agent integrations across channels with internal-system actions are close to his webhook and automation work.

stories.title: Skyscanner plans to cut 150 jobs, about 10% of staff, as AI changes travel search
stories.summary: Software development and middle-management roles are among those reportedly affected, alongside marketing, commercial, workplace and strategy teams.
stories.why: Another sign that AI-driven restructuring is hitting software teams, so a visible portfolio of shipped work matters.

stories.title: Pipedrive notifies Estonia of 236 layoffs and plans to close Lisbon and Prague offices
stories.summary: The cuts equal 62% of its 380 staff in Estonia, out of nearly 800 employees in total; developers in Berlin are also affected.
stories.why: A reminder that European product companies are consolidating, which can shrink hiring there.

stories.title: Vodafone Group plans data centres in Kenya through Vodafone Business
stories.summary: Kenya and Egypt are the next countries after a 4 MW facility opened in Izmir, Turkey, in September; Vodafone has not said whether Vodacom, Safaricom's parent, is a partner.
stories.why: More local compute for cloud and AI workloads, and a possible source of Nairobi infrastructure roles.

stories.title: Safaricom restores M-PESA GlobalPay virtual card after a two-day technical fault
stories.summary: Safaricom said on 23 November that a technical issue affected the virtual Visa card; on 25 November M-PESA said the service is back, with no cause given.
stories.why: A real example of a payments outage on a wallet-funded card, useful when thinking about retries and status messaging.
